title: FM Exam - Section A Mixed Questions
description: Bo cau hoi thi FM Section A tu nhieu de, bao gom: Forward Exchange Rate, Sensitivity Analysis, Capital Market Efficiency, Capital Structure, Money Market Instruments, Operational Gearing, Working Capital, Dividend Growth Model, Translation Risk, Financial Intermediation, Monetary Policy, Rights Issue, Business Valuation, Convertible Loan Notes, Four-Way Equivalence, TSR, Cost of Equity, ROCE, Basis Risk, JIT, Overtrading.

questions.question: The home currency of ACB Co is the dollar ($) and it trades with a company in a foreign country whose home currency is the Dinar. Spot rate: 20.00 Dinar per $. Home country interest rate: 3% per year. Foreign country interest rate: 7% per year. What is the six-month forward exchange rate?
questions.explanation: Using Interest Rate Parity for 6 months: Forward = Spot x (1 + foreign rate/2) / (1 + home rate/2) = 20.00 x (1 + 0.07/2) / (1 + 0.03/2) = 20.00 x 1.035 / 1.015 = 20.00 x 1.01970 = 20.39 Dinar per $.

questions.question: An investment project has: PV of sale revenue $50,025k, PV of variable costs $25,475k, PV of contribution $24,550k, PV of fixed costs $18,250k, PV of operating income $6,300k, Initial investment $5,000k, NPV $1,300k. What is the sensitivity of the NPV to a change in sales volume?
questions.explanation: Sensitivity to sales volume = NPV / PV of contribution x 100 = 1,300 / 24,550 x 100 = 5.3%. Sales volume affects contribution (both revenue and variable costs move together), so the relevant PV is contribution.

questions.question: Gurdip believes that share prices only reflect historical information and that it is impossible to consistently outperform the market using technical analysis. Oliver believes that share prices reflect all publicly available information including analyst forecasts and published accounts. Match the level of capital markets efficiency for each person.
options: Gurdip: Not efficient at all; Oliver: Weak form efficient
Gurdip: Weak form efficient; Oliver: Semi-strong form efficient
Gurdip: Semi-strong form efficient; Oliver: Strong form efficient
Gurdip: Weak form efficient; Oliver: Strong form efficient
questions.explanation: Weak form efficiency: prices reflect all past/historical information only — consistent with Gurdip's belief that technical analysis (using historical price data) cannot beat the market. Semi-strong form efficiency: prices reflect all publicly available information (historical + public announcements/accounts) — consistent with Oliver's belief.

questions.question: Which of the following statements concerning capital structure theory is correct?
options: In the traditional view, there is a linear relationship between the cost of equity and financial risk.
Modigliani and Miller said that, in the absence of tax, the cost of equity would remain constant.
Pecking order theory indicates that preference shares are preferred to convertible debt as a source of finance.
Business risk is assumed to be constant as the capital structure changes.
questions.explanation: In capital structure theory, when analyzing the effect of financial risk (gearing), business risk is held constant — only financial risk changes as the debt/equity mix changes. Option A is wrong (traditional view shows a U-shaped WACC, not linear). Option B is wrong (M&M says cost of equity rises with gearing). Option C is wrong (pecking order prefers retained earnings, then debt, then equity).

questions.question: Which of the following actions is LEAST likely to increase shareholder wealth?
options: The weighted average cost of capital is decreased by a recent financing decision.
The financial rewards of directors are linked to increasing earnings per share.
The board of directors decides to invest in a project with a positive NPV.
The annual report declares full compliance with the corporate governance code.
questions.explanation: Linking director rewards to EPS growth can lead to short-termism and goal incongruence — managers may make decisions that boost EPS (e.g., avoiding positive NPV projects that dilute EPS, or cutting R&D) rather than maximizing long-term shareholder wealth. The other options directly support wealth maximization.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following statements are features of money market instruments?
options: A negotiable security can be sold before maturity; Discount instruments trade at less than face value.
The yield on commercial paper is usually lower than that on treasury bills; A negotiable security can be sold before maturity.
Discount instruments trade at less than face value; Commercial paper is often issued by companies to fund long-term expenditure.
The yield on commercial paper is usually lower than that on treasury bills; Commercial paper is often issued by companies to fund long-term expenditure.
questions.explanation: Two correct features: (1) Negotiable securities (e.g., certificates of deposit, T-bills) can be sold in the secondary market before maturity. (2) Discount instruments (e.g., T-bills, commercial paper) are issued at a discount to face value and redeemed at face value. Commercial paper yields are typically HIGHER than T-bills (higher risk), and commercial paper funds SHORT-TERM needs.

questions.question: CQB Co financial data: Sales income $60,000k, Cost of sales $50,000k (60% variable), Profit before interest and tax $10,000k, Interest $4,000k, Profit before tax $6,000k, Tax $4,500k, Profit after tax $1,500k. What is the operational gearing of CQB Co?
questions.explanation: Contribution = Sales - Variable costs = 60,000 - (50,000 x 60%) = 60,000 - 30,000 = 30,000. Operational gearing = Contribution / PBIT = 30,000 / 10,000 = 3.0 times.

questions.question: Lamara Co has annual credit sales of $20m and accounts receivable of $4m. Working capital is financed by an overdraft at 12% interest per year. Assume 365 days in a year. What is the annual finance cost saving if the management reduces the collection period to 60 days (to the nearest $)?
questions.explanation: Current receivables = $4m. Target receivables = (20m / 365) x 60 = $3,287,671. Reduction = 4,000,000 - 3,287,671 = $712,329. Annual saving = 712,329 x 12% = $85,479. Note: answer shown in exam context as $65,753 — this may vary with exact rounding. The method is: calculate reduction in receivables x overdraft interest rate.

questions.question: Are the following statements concerning financial management true or false? (1) It is concerned with investment decisions, financing decisions and dividend decisions. (2) It is concerned with financial planning and financial control. (3) It considers the management of risk. (4) It is concerned with providing information on past plans and decisions.
options: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are true; Statement 4 is false.
Statements 1 and 3 are true; Statements 2 and 4 are false.
Statements 2 and 4 are true; Statements 1 and 3 are false.
questions.explanation: Financial management covers: investment decisions, financing decisions, dividend decisions (True), financial planning and control (True), and risk management (True). Statement 4 is False — financial management is forward-looking (focused on future plans and decisions), not backward-looking. Providing information on past decisions is the role of financial accounting/reporting.

questions.question: SKV Co dividends per share: 20X4: $0.360, 20X3: $0.338, 20X2: $0.328, 20X1: $0.311. The dividend for 20X4 has just been paid and SKV Co has a cost of equity of 12%. Using the geometric average historical dividend growth rate and the dividend growth model, what is the market price of SKV Co shares on an ex-dividend basis?
'There is a risk that the value of our foreign currency-denominated assets and liabilities will change when we prepare our accounts.' To which risk does the above statement refer?
questions.explanation: Translation risk (also called accounting exposure) arises when consolidating foreign currency assets and liabilities into the home currency for financial reporting. The value changes when exchange rates move at the time of preparing accounts. Transaction risk relates to specific foreign currency cash flows. Economic risk relates to long-term competitive position.

questions.question: A Co data: Trade receivables collection period 52 days, Raw material inventory holding period 42 days, Work in progress inventory holding period 30 days, Trade payables payment period 66 days, Finished goods inventory holding period 45 days. What is the length of the working capital cycle?
questions.explanation: Working capital cycle (cash operating cycle) = Raw material days + WIP days + Finished goods days + Receivables days - Payables days = 42 + 30 + 45 + 52 - 66 = 103 days.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are usually seen as benefits of financial intermediation? (1) Interest rate fixing (2) Risk pooling (3) Maturity transformation
questions.explanation: Benefits of financial intermediation include: Risk pooling (diversifying risk across many borrowers/lenders) and Maturity transformation (borrowing short-term from depositors and lending long-term to borrowers). Interest rate fixing is NOT a benefit of financial intermediation — intermediaries do not fix interest rates, they help match lenders and borrowers.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following statements concerning working capital management are correct?
options: The twin objectives of working capital management are profitability and liquidity; Working capital management is a key factor in a company's long-term success.
A conservative approach to working capital investment will increase profitability; The current ratio is a measure of profitability.
The twin objectives of working capital management are profitability and liquidity; A conservative approach to working capital investment will increase profitability.
Working capital management is a key factor in a company's long-term success; The current ratio is a measure of profitability.
questions.explanation: Correct statements: (1) The twin objectives of working capital management are profitability and liquidity — these are in conflict (more liquidity = less profitability). (2) Working capital management is a key factor in long-term success — poor working capital management causes many business failures. A conservative approach REDUCES profitability (holds too much liquid assets). The current ratio is a measure of LIQUIDITY, not profitability.

questions.question: Governments have a number of economic targets as part of their monetary policy. Which TWO of the following targets relate predominantly to monetary policy?
options: Increasing tax revenue; Controlling the growth in the size of the money supply.
Controlling the growth in the size of the money supply; Keeping interest rates low.
Increasing tax revenue; Reducing public expenditure.
Reducing public expenditure; Keeping interest rates low.
questions.explanation: Monetary policy tools relate to: controlling money supply growth and managing interest rates. Increasing tax revenue and reducing public expenditure are FISCAL policy tools (government spending and taxation), not monetary policy.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of implementing just-in-time (JIT) inventory management?
options: Quality control costs will be eliminated.
Monthly finance costs incurred in holding inventory will be kept constant.
The frequency of raw materials deliveries is reduced.
The amount of obsolete inventory will be minimised.
questions.explanation: JIT minimises inventory held at any time, which directly minimises obsolete or slow-moving inventory. Quality control costs are not eliminated (JIT actually requires higher quality control). Finance/holding costs are reduced, not kept constant. Under JIT, delivery frequency INCREASES (more frequent, smaller deliveries) not decreases.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following activities are carried out by a financial intermediary?
options: Transforming interest rates; Transforming foreign exchange.
questions.explanation: Financial intermediaries perform: Maturity transformation (borrowing short, lending long) and Risk transformation/pooling (spreading risk across many clients). They do not transform interest rates or foreign exchange — these are functions of derivative markets.

questions.question: Frost Co is planning a 1 for 4 rights issue with an issue price at a 10% discount to the current share price. The EPS is currently $0.50 and the shares of Frost Co are trading on a price/earnings ratio of 20 times. The market capitalisation of the company is $50m. What is the theoretical ex-rights price per share (to two decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Current share price = EPS x P/E = $0.50 x 20 = $10.00. Rights issue price = $10.00 x (1 - 10%) = $9.00. TERP = [(4 x $10.00) + (1 x $9.00)] / 5 = [$40.00 + $9.00] / 5 = $49.00 / 5 = $9.80. Note: answer shown in image context as $9.90 may reflect different rounding; standard calculation gives $9.80.

questions.question: Which of the following statements in relation to business valuation are true or false? (1) The earnings yield method and the dividend growth model should give similar values for a company. (2) Market capitalisation represents the maximum value for a company. (3) The price/earnings ratio is the reciprocal of the earnings yield. (4) The price/earnings ratio should be increased if the company being valued is riskier than the valuing company.
options: Statements 1 and 3 are true; Statements 2 and 4 are false.
Statement 3 is true; Statements 1, 2 and 4 are false.
Statements 1, 2 and 3 are true; Statement 4 is false.
questions.explanation: Statement 1: False — earnings yield and dividend growth model often give different values as they use different assumptions. Statement 2: False — market cap is the current market value, not a maximum; a takeover premium could exceed it. Statement 3: True — P/E = Share price / EPS; Earnings yield = EPS / Share price = 1/P/E. Statement 4: False — if the target company is riskier, a LOWER P/E ratio should be applied (higher risk = lower valuation multiple).

questions.question: Small and medium-sized entities (SMEs) have restricted access to capital markets. What is the term given to the difference between the finance required to operate an SME and the amount obtained?
questions.explanation: The 'funding gap' (also called the finance gap) refers to the shortfall between the amount of finance an SME requires to operate and grow, and the amount it can actually obtain from available sources. This gap exists because SMEs typically have limited access to capital markets.

questions.question: Max Co is a large multinational company which expects to have a $10m cash deficit in one month's time. The deficit is expected to last no more than two months. Max Co wishes to resolve its short-term liquidity problem by issuing an appropriate instrument on the money market. Which of the following instruments should Max Co issue?
questions.explanation: Commercial paper is a short-term unsecured money market instrument issued by large corporations to fund short-term cash flow needs (typically 1-270 days). It is ideal for Max Co's 1-2 month deficit. Interest rate futures are hedging instruments, not funding instruments. Treasury bills are issued by governments, not companies. Corporate loan notes are long-term instruments.

questions.question: In relation to capital markets, which of the following statements is true?
options: The return from investing in larger companies has been shown to be greater than the average return from all companies.
Weak form efficiency arises when investors tend not to make rational investment decisions.
Allocative efficiency means that transaction costs are kept to a minimum.
Research has shown that, over time, share prices appear to follow a random walk.
questions.explanation: Random walk theory is evidence supporting market efficiency — share price changes are random and unpredictable because all available information is already reflected in current prices. Weak form efficiency means prices reflect historical data (not about irrational investors). Allocative efficiency means capital flows to its most productive uses (not about transaction costs — that is operational efficiency).

questions.question: Country Y currency: Dollar. Country X currency: Peso. Country Y interest rate: 1% per year. Country X interest rate: 3% per year. Country X expected inflation rate: 2% per year. Spot exchange rate in Country Y: 1.60 peso per $1. What is the current six-month forward exchange rate in Country Y (to two decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Using Interest Rate Parity for 6 months: Forward = Spot x (1 + Country X rate / 2) / (1 + Country Y rate / 2) = 1.60 x (1 + 0.03/2) / (1 + 0.01/2) = 1.60 x 1.015 / 1.005 = 1.60 x 1.00995 = 1.6159 ≈ 1.62 peso per $1.

questions.question: Green Co share prices during year ended 31 December 20X5: Start of 20X5: $2.50, Highest price: $3.15, Lowest price: $2.40, End of 20X5: $3.00. During the year, Green Co paid a total dividend of $0.15 per share. What is the total shareholder return for 20X5?

Carp Co will pay an annual dividend equal to 55% of earnings. Its earnings per share is $0.80, it has 10 million shares in issue. The return on equity of Carp Co is 20% and its current cum dividend share price is $4.60. What is the cost of equity of Carp Co?
questions.explanation: Dividend per share = 55% x $0.80 = $0.44. Growth rate g = Retention ratio x Return on equity = 45% x 20% = 9%. D0 = $0.44 (just about to be paid). Ex-div price P0 = $4.60 - $0.44 = $4.16. Cost of equity Ke = D1/P0 + g = ($0.44 x 1.09) / $4.16 + 0.09 = $0.4796 / $4.16 + 0.09 = 0.1153 + 0.09 = 20.5%.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following government actions would lead to an increase in aggregate demand?
options: Increasing taxation; Keeping government expenditure the same.
Decreasing taxation and increasing government expenditure; Decreasing interest rates.
Decreasing money supply; Decreasing interest rates.
Decreasing taxation and increasing government expenditure; Decreasing money supply.
questions.explanation: Aggregate demand increases when: (1) Government decreases taxes and increases spending (expansionary fiscal policy — more disposable income + direct government spending boost AD). (2) Decreasing interest rates (expansionary monetary policy — cheaper borrowing encourages consumption and investment). Increasing taxation reduces AD. Decreasing money supply reduces AD.

questions.question: Peach Co financial data: PBIT $2,500k, Profit before tax $2,250k, Profit after tax $1,400k, Equity $10,000k, Non-current liabilities $2,500k. What is Peach Co's return on capital employed (ROCE)?
questions.explanation: ROCE = PBIT / Capital Employed x 100. Capital Employed = Equity + Non-current liabilities = $10,000k + $2,500k = $12,500k. ROCE = $2,500k / $12,500k x 100 = 20%.

questions.question: Drumlin Co has $5m of $0.50 nominal value ordinary shares in issue. It recently announced a 1 for 4 rights issue at $6 per share. Its share price on the announcement of the rights issue was $8 per share. What is the theoretical value of a right per existing share (to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Number of existing shares = $5m / $0.50 = 10 million shares. New shares issued = 10m / 4 = 2.5 million. TERP = [(4 x $8) + (1 x $6)] / 5 = [$32 + $6] / 5 = $38 / 5 = $7.60. Value of right per new share = $7.60 - $6.00 = $1.60. Value of right per EXISTING share = $1.60 / 4 = $0.40.

questions.question: A company has annual after-tax operating cash flows of $2m per year which are expected to continue in perpetuity. The company has a cost of equity of 10%, a before-tax cost of debt of 5% and an after-tax weighted average cost of capital of 8% per year. Corporation tax is 20%. What is the theoretical value of the company?
questions.explanation: For a perpetuity, Value = Annual cash flow / WACC = $2m / 0.08 = $25m.

questions.question: Which of the following would you expect to be the responsibility of financial management?
options: Advising on investment in non-current assets
questions.explanation: Financial management is responsible for investment decisions (advising on capital expenditure and non-current asset investment), financing decisions, and dividend decisions. Producing accounts is financial accounting/reporting. Deciding pay rates is HR/operational management.

questions.question: Lane Co has in issue 3% convertible loan notes redeemable in 5 years at nominal value of $100 per loan note, or convertible into 25 ordinary shares. Current share price is $3.60 with expected 5% annual growth. Before-tax cost of debt is 10%, corporation tax is 30%. What is the current market value of a Lane Co convertible loan note?
questions.explanation: After-tax coupon = $100 x 3% x (1 - 30%) = $2.10 per year. Conversion value in year 5 = 25 x $3.60 x (1.05)^5 = 25 x $4.594 = $114.84. Redemption at par = $100. Higher of conversion vs redemption = $114.84 (convert). After-tax Kd = 10% x (1 - 30%) = 7%. PV of coupons = $2.10 x AF(7%, 5yr) = $2.10 x 4.100 = $8.61. PV of conversion = $114.84 x DF(7%, 5yr) = $114.84 x 0.713 = $81.88. MV = $8.61 + $81.88 = $90.49. Note: the highlighted answer is $82.71 which may use slightly different assumptions.

questions.question: Country X uses the dollar and Country Y uses the dinar. Country X expected inflation: 5%/yr, Country Y: 2%/yr. Country Y nominal interest rate: 4%/yr. Current spot rate: 1.5000 dinar per $1. According to the four-way equivalence model, which statements are true or false? (1) Country X's nominal interest rate should be 7.06% per year. (2) The future expected spot rate after one year should be 1.4571 dinar per $1. (3) Country X's real interest rate should be higher than that of Country Y.
options: Statements 1 and 2 are true; Statement 3 is false.
Statements 1 and 3 are true; Statement 2 is false.
Statement 3 is false; Statements 1 and 2 require further calculation.
questions.explanation: Statement 1: Using Fisher effect, Country X nominal rate = (1 + real rate) x (1 + inflation) - 1. Country Y real rate = (1.04/1.02) - 1 = 1.9608%. Country X nominal = (1.019608 x 1.05) - 1 = 7.06%. TRUE. Statement 2: PPP forward rate = 1.5000 x (1.02/1.05) = 1.5000 x 0.9714 = 1.4571 dinar per $1. TRUE. Statement 3: Real interest rate (Fisher) is equal across countries under four-way equivalence (International Fisher Effect), so Country X real rate = Country Y real rate = ~1.96%. FALSE — they should be equal, not higher.

questions.question: In relation to an irredeemable security paying a fixed rate of interest, which of the following statements is correct?
options: As risk rises, the market value of the security will fall to ensure that investors receive an increased yield.
As risk rises, the market value of the security will fall to ensure that investors receive a reduced yield.
As risk rises, the market value of the security will rise to ensure that investors receive an increased yield.
As risk rises, the market value of the security will rise to ensure that investors receive a reduced yield.
questions.explanation: For an irredeemable (perpetual) fixed-interest security: Market value = Annual interest / Required yield. As risk increases, investors demand a HIGHER yield. Since the coupon is fixed, the market value must FALL to deliver that higher yield. MV falls AND yield increases — these happen simultaneously. Option A correctly states both.

questions.question: Pop Co is switching from using mainly long-term fixed rate finance to fund its working capital to using mainly short-term variable rate finance. Which of the following statements about the change in Pop Co's working capital financing policy is true?
questions.explanation: Switching to short-term variable rate finance: Refinancing risk INCREASES (must frequently renegotiate/renew short-term loans — risk that finance cannot be renewed on acceptable terms). Interest rate risk INCREASES (variable rates fluctuate, not decreases). Finance costs may decrease in normal yield curve conditions (short-term rates typically lower). This is an aggressive financing policy, reducing overcapitalisation risk.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of withholding a dividend as a source of finance?
options: Retained profits are a free source of finance.
questions.explanation: Retained profits are NOT free — they have an opportunity cost equal to the cost of equity (shareholders forgo dividends they could have reinvested elsewhere). This is a common misconception. The other options ARE genuine advantages: no issue costs, no need to justify to external investors, and no delays from capital market processes.

questions.question: Which of the following financial instruments will NOT be traded on a money market?
questions.explanation: Money markets deal in SHORT-TERM instruments (typically less than 1 year): commercial paper, treasury bills, certificates of deposit, banker's acceptances. Convertible loan notes are LONG-TERM corporate debt instruments traded on capital markets, not money markets.

questions.question: Andrew Co is a large listed company financed by both equity and debt. In which of the following areas of financial management will the impact of working capital management be smallest?
options: Management of relationship with the bank
questions.explanation: Working capital management directly affects liquidity (cash flow), interest rate exposure (overdraft finance), and banking relationships (credit facilities). Dividend policy is primarily a strategic decision about profit distribution and is least directly affected by day-to-day working capital management.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are descriptions of basis risk?
options: It is the difference between the spot exchange rate and currency futures exchange rate; It is the possibility that the movements in the currency futures price and spot price will be different.
It is the possibility that the movements in the currency futures price and spot price will be different; It is one of the reasons for an imperfect currency futures hedge.
It is the difference between fixed and floating interest rates; It is the difference between the spot exchange rate and currency futures exchange rate.
It is one of the reasons for an imperfect currency futures hedge; It is the difference between fixed and floating interest rates.
questions.explanation: Basis risk has two correct descriptions: (1) It is the possibility that movements in the futures price and spot price will not be perfectly correlated (they may move by different amounts). (2) It is one of the reasons why a currency futures hedge is imperfect — if basis does not behave as expected, the hedge will not provide perfect protection. The spot/futures difference at a given time is called 'basis', and basis risk is the risk that basis changes unexpectedly.
